reviews.title: DUMB!
reviews.text:
I’m giving a low rating because the instructor in my very first Spanish video claimed that for a fluent English speaker, Spanish is easy to learn because they are both Latin languages.
First of all, the correct term is Romance language (the only Latin language is straight-up Latin!). Second, while Spanish is a Romance language, English most certainly is not. Yes, English was heavily influenced by French (a Romance language) after the 1066 Norman Conquest, which gave us a lot of borrowed vocabulary. However, English is fundamentally a GERMANIC language. Despite the borrowed Latin words, our grammar, syntax, sentence structure, and most common, everyday words (like water, house, strong, I, you) remain distinctly Germanic. If I were learning German, and the instructor told me it might be easier to learn because of our shared roots, that would be accurate.
Also it’s trying to teach me that “el” means both the and he. But he is “Él” so they shouldn’t treat that as the came. This made me laugh.

reviews.title: Has promise
reviews.text:
It’s a fun and cute and a little bit addictive app (this is a good thing in a learning app) but not really there yet. A bit amateur and sloppy and I suspect very AI influenced. . It’s not always intuitive how sections work. It adds erroneous words like people’s names and letter pronunciations to its flip cards. It isolates phrases for the listener to repeat but often includes the last word from the previous sentence. I definitely feel like it’s on the right track, but I don’t have time for all these errors right now. If I was learning just for fun I might try longer, but I don’t so I am switching to another app.

Edit: to people complaining about it costing money—seriously? Are you providing free apps? Sure that would be nice but I do not expect people to work for free. Also, it’s very easy to cancel during the trial week. Just go to your Apple subscriptions. If you missed that you have just seven days free, that’s on you.

reviews.title: Great Concept - Poor Execution
reviews.text:
I was excited to start using Parrot because I love the idea of tools that it adds on top of other popular Spanish immersion apps (e.g. D.S). Unfortunately, the app has been unreliable for me and the quality of content is not as high as other apps. 

My biggest complaint is that key features in the app oftentimes just randomly won’t work.  I often have to highlight phrases multiple times before the app will translate them. The typical response is that it just says “Parroting” and won’t give a translation. It eventually does work if I try multiple times on the same phrase, but that’s frustrating.  Besides that, flashcards are glitchy sometimes, and I have also had individual videos that would not play. 

Less important, but still worth mentioning, is that the quality of a lot of the videos is pretty mid. I’m on about the 12th lesson, and I find many of the videos to be unengaging. The writing / storylines are uninteresting, the acting is poor, and the sound quality is amateurish. 

Parrot has the core for a great app. It’s just not there yet.

reviews.title: Subscription and Scams
reviews.text:
The app presentation is well put together, but the inability to access subscriptions on the app, website or App Store is widely concerning. The issue with it forcing a subscription for everything as well is off putting; I even had an recent issue with it picking a yearly subscription when the monthly was clearly pushed. There was no email or notification about the trial ending early, or that it’d charge soon. I wasn’t made aware of the amount till after it hit the bank account, which was incorrect in my previous statement. 

All of this is very disappointing in an app, especially with being so excited about the way it teaches Spanish.

I got the app, and it said free? But it set a plan up and I couldn’t exit out of it! 🥲 I was looking forward to using this and couldn’t so I was a little disappointed I would still be interested in using it but I don’t want to pay! I thought it was free…

reviews.text:
It was an amazing app until
I payed lol, or moved further in progress... Lessons became shorter, don’t have time to memorize things. Pronunciation on click or after tasks (how it used to be on first lessons) disappeared. Same with phrases/words explanations after you choose the correct answer. There is no system that helps you with word learning, it just shows you words in order you saved them until you click that you remember it, they assume you will learn it during lessons, but they don’t repeat at all (except of basic ones). I don’t see a huge difference from Duolingo’s free version with using TikTok/youtube and they claimed it’s way better.. $100 for nothing. 

Just started another lesson after writing this review and the video didn’t have doubt at all..

reviews.title: Not Real Clear How to Progress
reviews.text: Doulingo has its drawbacks, but in general you know when you should move forward or how to move forward. With Parrot I often found I did not know what I was suppose to be doing or working on, or why the next lesson was open, or when the previous lesson was done. Maybe there are no actually lessons. Some sort of instructions would have been helpful. The developer was very responsive and did give me some pointers - but I shouldn’t need to contact the developer. A simple link to a YouTube video on how to use the product as intended would have helped a great deal. Neither was I able to figure out how to use flash cards, or how to control what is included in a flash card deck. I wanted to practice some words with flash cards, but could not figure out how to control the content. Also, when playing a video you can click on a word to see its definition which is nice, but I did not understand the color coding or how to change the color coding - like if I accidentally clicked to indicate I knew a word, how do you undo that. I ended up feeling confused and pretty dumb - I’m just trying to learn Spanish, and I’m getting stuck on just trying to figure out how to use the app. Probably great for young folk in their 20s.
